title: Web and HTTP for CRUD Apps
description: The HTTP knowledge every CRUD app depends on: request and response messages, methods, status codes, REST resource design, validation and problem details, filtering and paging, authentication vs authorization, cookies, JWTs, password hashing, CSRF, CORS, caching with ETags, rate limiting, webhooks, versioning, and correlation IDs. Runnable TypeScript exercises model each rule as a small pure function, with ASP.NET Core examples alongside.
outcomes: Read raw HTTP requests and responses and explain what each line and header does
Choose methods and status codes correctly, including safe vs idempotent methods and Idempotency-Key retries
Design resource URLs, and use PUT, PATCH (JSON Merge Patch), 201 + Location, and 204 correctly
Return consistent problem details errors and validate request bodies in layers (415, 400, 409)
Build list endpoints with allow-listed filters, stable sorting, capped paging, and Link headers
Tell authentication from authorization and pick 401, 403, or 404
Configure session cookies (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, __Host-) and explain what a JWT contains and why it holds no secrets
Explain password hashing with salts, work factors, constant-time comparison, and rehash-on-login
Explain CSRF, how SameSite and anti-forgery tokens stop it, and what CORS does and does not protect
Use Cache-Control, ETags, If-None-Match/304, and If-Match/412 for caching and optimistic concurrency
Apply rate limiting with 429/Retry-After, verify signed webhooks, version an API, and trace requests with correlation IDs
